All three report **at least 16 wounded** (CBC, CNN, VoxNews) and none mention an arrest; the perpetrator is described as a former student who either killed himself or was later identified (Omer Ket). 2. **Inference** – Because the only publicly‑available outlets that have been indexed so far give a casualty figure of 16 (or “at least 16”), they contradict the council’s hypothesis that “eleven people are wounded”. No source in the archive or elsewhere reports a figure of 11, nor a different date or a narrative in which the shooter is arrested. 3. **Uncertainty** – It is possible that other outlets (local Turkish newspapers, regional TV stations, or later updates) have reported a different number (e.g., 12‑15) or that an arrest was announced after the initial reports. Those sources have not yet been captured in the system, so the answer is limited to the evidence presently available. **Concrete Test** - **Step 1:** Query the *wikipedia‑current‑events* stream for the date range surrounding the incident (e.g., 2026‑04‑10 to 2026‑04‑20) with the keywords “Turgutlu”, “high school”, “shooting”, “wounded”, “arrest”. - **Step 2:** Retrieve the top‑5 results and extract any casualty figures, dates, and statements about the perpetrator’s status. - **Step 3:** Compare the extracted figures to the “eleven wounded” claim. If any result lists a number other than 11, a different date, or mentions an arrest, record it as a counter‑example; otherwise, confirm that current independent sources consistently report 16 wounded and no arrest. Executing this test will either validate the answer (no differing reports found) or reveal new evidence that modifies the conclusion.
